newsitem.title: USA: Motorola earnings fall in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Motorola earnings fall in quarter.

text.p: Motorola Inc. said Thursday it earned $238 million in the fourth quarter, down from $432 million in the 1995 quarter, hurt by restructuring costs that offset higher sales.
The maker of cellular phones, computer chips and other electronic gear said sales grew to $7.7 billion from $7.3 billion. Earnings per share fell to 39 cents from 72 cents.
The earnings were slightly below the 41 cents a share that Wall Street analysts had expected, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
For the year, Motorola said it earned $1.15 billion, down from $1.78 billion, on sales of $28.0 billion, up from $27.0 billion. Earnings per share fell to $1.90 from $2.93 for the year.
Motorola said earnings were reduced by $150 million in the quarter from restructuring and other one-time charges. The various charges had been announced last year.
It said its semiconductor business lost money in the quarter, though sales and orders for the key products grew in the quarter from the third quarter.
Motorola stock rose 62.5 cents to $64 on the New York Stock Exchange. The company released its results after the market closed. The shares rose to $65 in after-hours trading.
